articles.title: Chelsea staff warned over Fantasy Premier League use
articles.summary: Chelsea warn staff to be careful about revealing team news through Fantasy Premier League after Joao Pedro's injury appeared to have been inadvertently disclosed through team selections.
articles.body:
Chelsea have warned staff to be careful about inadvertently revealing team news through Fantasy Premier League after Joao Pedro's injury appeared to have been disclosed through team selections.

An email was sent to staff reminding them of the potential consequences of using inside information when playing Fantasy Premier League or other public gaming platforms, where team selection choices could reveal which players are unavailable or close to returning.

It followed leaks before the 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham , when Pedro was a surprise absentee because of what has since emerged to be a quad injury.

Several influential Fantasy Premier League content creators claimed to have seen evidence that forward Morgan Rogers, along with several members of Chelsea staff, had removed Pedro from their Fantasy Premier League teams before kick-off at Stamford Bridge, despite no club announcement having been made about his injury.

Asked about the matter by BBC Sport after the defeat, Xabi Alonso said he was unaware of the situation. He replied: "I am not into the fantasy team thing, so I didn't know that."

Since joining Chelsea in the summer, Alonso, 44, has generally been guarded when discussing injury issues in media conferences.

Chelsea have also previously experienced problems with leaks.

During former manager Liam Rosenior's four-month spell in charge last season, team selections were leaked before both legs of the club's Champions League defeat by Paris St-Germain.

It also later emerged former defender Marc Cucurella's barber had revealed on social media that Pedro and Cole Palmer would miss a trip to Brighton last season after discussing the matter with his client.

With regard to Fantasy Premier League, no further restrictions are expected because Chelsea regard the incident as an isolated case that can be managed through greater awareness among players and staff.

There have been many further examples, claiming to suggest players from clubs like Arsenal , Liverpool , Leicester and Newcastle made revealing changes to their teams, while BBC Sport has identified accounts believed by Fantasy Premier League trackers to be linked to high-profile players and figures at clubs across the division.

The highest-profile example was arguably the revelation of then Aston Villa forward Jack Grealish's omission from the squad before a match against Leicester City in February 2021.

Then Leicester manager Brendan Rodgers later said he had been aware of rumours surrounding Grealish's injury absence before the match, which his side won.

More than 11 million people are said to play Fantasy Premier League, which has become an increasingly prominent part of the wider football ecosystem.

Although there are strict rules prohibiting gambling, the Premier League offers no specific guidance to clubs on how, or whether, those involved in the game should participate in Fantasy Premier League.

Instead, it is generally treated as a matter for individual clubs to manage themselves.

articles.title: Raúl González Blanco, nuevo entrenador del Real Oviedo
articles.standfirst: El madrileño toma las riendas del club asturiano y vivirá su primera experiencia en Segunda
articles.summary: El madrileño toma las riendas del club asturiano y vivirá su primera experiencia en Segunda
articles.body: El Real Oviedo ya tiene nuevo entrenador. Raúl González Blanco se hará cargo del equipo asturiano después de que el club haya confirmado oficialmente su contratación. El técnico madrileño firma un contrato hasta el 30 de junio de 2028, por lo que se compromete con la entidad azul para lo que resta de esta temporada y la siguiente. La apuesta del Grupo Pachuca por el exentrenador del Real Madrid Castilla tiene, por tanto, un recorrido que va más allá de la presente campaña. "El Real Oviedo ha alcanzado un acuerdo para la contratación de Raúl González Blanco como nuevo entrenador del primer equipo hasta junio de 2028", señala el comunicado con el que la entidad asturiana ha anunciado la incorporación del sustituto de Julián Calero, destituido pese a la victoria conseguida el pasado fin de semana en Cádiz. El nombramiento de Raúl supone su estreno al frente de un primer equipo profesional después de desarrollar toda su trayectoria como entrenador en la cantera del Real Madrid. Desde su llegada a Valdebebas en 2018, pasó por diferentes categorías inferiores, conquistó la Liga de Campeones Juvenil en 2020 y dirigió durante seis temporadas al Castilla. El comunicado del Oviedo también recuerda su extraordinaria trayectoria como futbolista, especialmente en el Real Madrid, "equipo con el que se consagró y donde se convirtió en una leyenda tras más de 15 años defendiendo la elástica blanca". El club confirma igualmente que Raúl "dirigirá su primer partido como nuevo entrenador azul este próximo sábado ante el Girona en el Carlos Tartiere". La presentación será este martes a las 13:30 horas.

articles.title: "No ha habido efecto Aguirre, se me agotan las palabras para justificar lo injustificable"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Valencia lamenta que no han llegado los resultados, aunque considera que ve cosas buenas y evolución en el equipo
articles.summary: El técnico del Valencia lamenta que no han llegado los resultados, aunque considera que ve cosas buenas y evolución en el equipo
articles.body: Javier Aguirre admite que su llegada al banquillo del Valencia todavía no ha tenido el impacto esperado en los resultados. El técnico mexicano, en la víspera del partido de Copa ante el Tavernes, reconoció que "no ha habido efecto Aguirre" tras sumar una victoria en cinco jornadas de Liga, defendió que el equipo ha mejorado en aspectos como el juego y la actitud respecto a sus primeros partidos al frente del conjunto blanquinegro y aseguró que se le "agotan las palabras para justificar lo injustificable". Pese a la delicada situación clasificatoria, Aguirre se mostró convencido de que el trabajo realizado acabará dando resultados y apeló al esfuerzo diario para revertir la dinámica del equipo. ¿Se está convirtiendo este Valencia en uno de los retos más complicados de su carrera? “He tenido buenos retos en mi carrera. Este es uno de los buenos, claro que sí. Es un histórico de España y de Europa, y es un bonito reto, claro que sí. No lo dudé, ya lo dije hace un mes, cuando llegué. Había que venir aquí, había que hacer bien las cosas. Estamos en ello, estamos en ello. Está siendo lento, pero estamos encontrando cosas buenas. Hemos mejorado los entrenamientos, pero no se han traducido en buenos resultados, que es lo que nos interesa, y seguimos en una zona muy complicada. Pero seguiremos trabajando”. Han pasado cinco partidos de Liga, con cinco puntos y tres rivales duros: Villarreal, Athletic Club y Real Madrid. ¿Es lo que esperaba? ¿Cree que con el alivio del calendario llegarán los puntos? “No, esperaba más. En resultados esperaba más. Necesitaba un par de puntos más; eso es lo que esperaba. Mi experiencia me dice que no puedo mirar más allá de Tavernes ahora y del Rayo, después del parón liguero. Esa es la verdad. Ustedes tienen una buena frase que yo no uso en México: las cuentas de la lechera a vender humo, como también se dice. Bueno, tres puntos aquí, dos allá… Esos presupuestos, según mi experiencia, no conducen a nada. Es el día a día. Acuñó la frase mi amigo Cholo: partido a partido. Y es verdad. Y es verdad. No puedes ver más allá de ese partido. 'Bueno, sí, está bien, perdemos con el Barça, con el Madrid, pero le ganamos al Rayo'. No; son cuentas de la lechera, exactamente.” ¿Qué ha pasado con el 'efecto Aguirre'? Usted ha dicho que el proceso está siendo lento. ¿Por qué le está costando al equipo? “Porque no tenemos buenos resultados. Eso. ¿Por qué no tenemos buenos resultados? ¿Usted analiza los resultados? ¿Recuerda usted el Santander? [La ocasión fallada por Hugo Duro] ¿Qué pasó al final del partido, contra el Villarreal, en el noventa y tantos? ¡Pum! Otro punto. El efecto Aguirre, o lo que usted menciona, se hubiera adornado mejor con 12 puntos y en el puesto 11 o 12 de la Liga. La conclusión es el gol: que no te hagan gol aquí y meterlo allí. Ese es el efecto Aguirre: los resultados. Y los resultados no me favorecen en absoluto. Por lo tanto, no ha habido efecto Aguirre. Pero Aguirre trabaja en el campo buscando buenos resultados, y el trabajo de campo, que seguramente no ven, aunque se lo imaginan, es bueno. Hay progreso. Hay cosas buenas, como decía al compañero. Sinceramente, no se traducen en los resultados. Espero que tarde o temprano. ¿Qué es lo que interesa al final? Olvídate de que juegue bien, mal, regular o bonito. Hay que ganar, hay que ganar y hay que ganar. Es una máxima en el fútbol. Lo otro, bueno, sí, lo puedes adornar, pero es ganar. Y no hemos ganado. En cinco partidos hemos ganado una sola vez. No hay ni efectos ni historias. El equipo no ha funcionado en cuanto a resultados. Y hay que seguir trabajando. No tengo otra fórmula. Y se me agotan las palabras para justificar lo injustificable: no hemos ganado. Por lo tanto, no hay resultados tangibles en cuanto a puntos. Esa es una verdad como una catedral. Yo estoy feliz. Tengo que creerlo. Claro que sí. Me lastiman mucho, me duelen las lesiones: lo de Jesús Vázquez, lo de Otorbi. Son circunstancias que no me gustan. Que suceden, sí, es verdad que suceden. Pero eso es lo que más me cuesta asimilar después de tantos y tantos años. Yo, que estuve fuera diez meses con una fractura de tibia cuando jugaba al fútbol, sé que es el peor momento de la vida de un futbolista. Y como entrenador me duelen mucho las lesiones. Por lo demás, sé que con trabajo, con optimismo, con entusiasmo, con la actitud y la aptitud que tienen, esto saldrá adelante. Lo creo. Soy optimista desde el minuto uno hasta hoy”. Dijo que veía brotes verdes y que el equipo debía seguir esa senda para sumar puntos, 'si es posible, jugando bien'. ¿Qué es para usted jugar bien? “Saber qué hacer con la pelota y saber qué hacer sin ella. Eso es jugar bien. Saber exactamente qué tengo que hacer cuando tengo el balón y, cuando no lo tengo, lo mismo. Eso es jugar bien: el equilibrio del juego. A veces se juega bien y bonito. A veces no se juega bien ni bonito y se gana. A veces se juega bien y bonito y no se gana. A veces se juega mal: ¿por qué no tienes ideas?, ¿por qué no defiendes bien? Y cuenta que el rival también puede jugar bien, y que juega mejor que tú porque tiene más calidad, más tiempo juntos, más trabajo. Y luego, otra parte de la ecuación es el arbitraje. Al final hay un reglamento, a veces te condiciona su aplicación y ya está. Pero sí, jugar bien es eso: saber qué hacer. Que entre un jugador y sepa, en esa posición, qué quiere de él el entrenador, qué le pide el sistema de juego. Eso es jugar bien”. ¿En qué ve esos brotes verdes? ¿En la actitud, en el juego? “En actitud y en juego, en esas dos. En actitud, muy buena desde el calentamiento. Entramos bien al partido, y luego el partido se descompone. Al minuto 25 estábamos, a mi juicio, bastante igualados: un par de ocasiones de ellos, de nosotros, y luego se descompone con el gol. Ahí nos desequilibramos un poco emocionalmente. Y en juego, claro: hay más posesión de balón, tenemos más expectativa de gol. Eso es lo que yo veo. Los números no se traducen; el verdadero número es ganar o perder, no hay más. Y no hemos ganado. Te lo explico: en actitud y en juego. Defendemos mejor, creo yo, que el primer día en Santander. Creo que jugamos mejor que el primer día en Santander. Nos atrevemos más que el primer día en Santander. Todo es un cúmulo, para mí. Puedo respetar tu opinión si no estás de acuerdo; es bastante valiosa. Es lo que yo veo. Me atrevo a hacerlo público porque me lo preguntan, y ya está. Esa es mi opinión, y respeto que haya diferencias”. El Tavernes ha decidido jugar como local en Mestalla. ¿Habría sido mucho más complicado jugar allí, en Tavernes, sobre césped artificial? “Sin lugar a dudas, porque es otra superficie. Partiendo de esa base lógica, el bote del balón… De entrada, hubiéramos entrenado en otro campo que no fuera de hierba natural. Sin lugar a dudas, habría habido que adaptarse a las botas, al balón, al bote, al entorno o, mejor dicho, al escenario de jugar como visitante en un campo que desconocemos. Hubiéramos tenido que prepararnos de otra manera o entrenar de otra manera. Estoy de acuerdo con usted. Ellos aceptaron de buena gana jugar como local en Mestalla y lo agradecemos, porque va a ir más gente y va a ser un ambiente festivo, tipo Copa del Rey de toda la vida. A un solo partido, y a ver cómo lo afrontamos, a ver cómo estamos. La Copa no ha estorbado en lo absoluto. Me ha tocado estar en dos finales de Copa y es una competición muy bonita, que da vida a muchos equipos que no tienen tanta visibilidad como los de Primera. Son partidos de verdad; ha habido sorpresas enormes que todos recordamos en la Copa del Rey. Hay un premio, jugar la Supercopa. En fin, la Copa es muy atractiva. No es ningún estorbo en lo absoluto. Fue una pena que, por aquel accidente ferroviario, tengamos que jugar hasta ahora, pero lo afrontamos con mucho respeto y con mucha seriedad”. En este tipo de eliminatorias el equipo de Primera suele ganar cómodamente. ¿Se pueden sacar conclusiones positivas ante un equipo semiprofesional como el Tavernes? “No sé si son semiprofesionales. No sé si cobran o no cobran. Es un equipo al que hay que respetar. Es un equipo de fútbol, está en su categoría, nos tocó por sorteo y algo hicieron bien para llegar a jugar contra un Primera División. Son partidos que recuerdas toda la vida. Cuando era futbolista jugué contra Maradona, contra Platini, y no se me olvida nunca. Con Cruyff me tocó jugar. Es la ilusión que te da el fútbol. Yo jugué la Copa del Rey, jugué en Mestalla. Nosotros tenemos que hacer un partido serio, respetar al rival, poner a los mejores, a los que creemos que deben jugar, respetando el reglamento, y hay que estar bien”. Gayá, expulsado, no podrá jugar el próximo partido de Liga, y Jesús está lesionado. ¿Apostará mañana por Gayá o dará la oportunidad a otro jugador, del filial o de la plantilla? “No, a Gayá no lo vamos a poner. Vamos a ver cómo lo resolvemos. Tenemos gente de sobra y, de momento, estoy tranquilo. Hay opciones para jugar: un perfil cambiado puede ser, o un central zurdo pegado a la izquierda. En ese sentido estoy tranquilo, porque la plantilla es amplia y hay jugadores que pueden jugar en distintas posiciones”. ¿Veremos más canteranos en el partido de Copa? “Más canteranos, yo lo explico. Nosotros teníamos convocados para el partido de Copa, antes del desgraciado momento de aquel accidente, al portero Raúl Jiménez, que siempre ha venido con nosotros. Tenemos canteranos ya prácticamente con dinámica de primer equipo, como Aimar, como Otorbi, como Iker Córdoba, como Mayol. Y ese día venían Gamón, Jaume Durá y Panach. Ellos tienen un partido aplazado el miércoles y juegan el domingo. El Mestalla también está sufriendo algunos resultados, está con ciertos agobios. Hemos hablado con su míster e intentaremos que los dos compromisos salgan bien. Los canteranos hacen su trabajo y lo mejor que pueden, con dinámica diaria: Mayol, Otorbi, Córdoba y Aimar. Creo que son jóvenes con mucho entusiasmo, y luego tenemos 24 fichas o así. No es fácil decidir. Qué bueno que no sea fácil decidir entre uno y otro. Insisto, no me gustan las lesiones, pero ahora tenemos a Otorbi y a Jesús fuera, más los internacionales que están con sus selecciones. Pero haremos un buen equipo para mañana, sin lugar a dudas, y un buen equipo para Vallecas”. Hugo Duro, Diakhaby y Harvey Elliott están teniendo poca participación en los últimos partidos, y son jugadores con un peso importante en la masa salarial del club. ¿Cómo ve su situación? ¿Pueden salir de inicio mañana, salvo Diakhaby, que está con su selección? “Diakhaby, cuando llegamos estaba lesionado, bien lesionado, y tenía para largo. Lo recuperamos y ahora va a su selección. Es un jugador que quiere mucho al club, que es un baluarte y que seguramente aparecerá dentro de poco, porque le faltaba un poco de ritmo de competición. Elliott también jugó en Santander, ha venido jugando. Hemos estado hablando con él para que mejore en algunas cosas y creo que lo ha hecho bien en los entrenamientos. Ojalá tenga posibilidad de jugar. Y Hugo Duro ha jugado, está ahí peleando. Volvió Sadiq, está ahí, y está Imar también. Tengo tres en ese puesto. Están bien, están disponibles y están entrenando bien. Diakhaby está con la selección; los otros dos pueden jugar mañana fácilmente”. Hace unos días dijo que estaba contento con Sato y que le daría oportunidades, pero contra el Madrid no fue convocado. ¿Cuál es su situación? “El chaval está como los otros, el 26 y el 27. Entrenan bien y hay que meter a 23 en la convocatoria. Siempre sobrarán cuatro; están todos sanos. Otorbi está fuera, y Jesús. Quedan 25, dos se quedarán fuera para el partido en Vallecas, y Sato está igual que todos. Está trabajando bien, está haciendo sus cosas y no caben todos. A veces están en el banquillo, a veces en el campo y a veces en la grada. El nivel es muy parejo entre todos”.

articles.title: Grading Every Premier League Team's 2026-27 Season So Far at the November International Break
articles.summary: It's been a topsy-turvy 10 games into the 2026-27 Premier League season.
articles.body:
It's been a topsy-turvy 10 games into the 2026-27 Premier League season.

There's little surprise seeing defending champions Arsenal at the top of the table. But Manchester United in the relegation zone must make fans of the Red Devils sick to their stomachs.

Brighton looks to break the hegemony at the top while sitting in second, while Liverpool, Chelsea, and Everton seem well-positioned to challenge for Champions League football next season.

As we head into the November international break, our Calum Rogers, Leo Collis, and Nick Akerman grade every single Premier League team's campaign so far.

Disagree with what they had to say? Submit your thoughts now in the comments section of the app!

So far, so good for the reigning Premier League champions.

While a 3-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion in the middle of September was an undoubted shock—which ended the Gunners' quest for another invincible season—the rest of their 10 matches have delivered nine victories, including wins over Aston Villa, Chelsea and Liverpool.

That has them sitting at the top of the Premier League, five points in front of the Seagulls and six points ahead of a Manchester City side expecting a significant points deduction.

A suffocating defense has been the foundation for success, with just five goals conceded. Arsenal have four 1-0 wins and two additional victories secured by a one-goal margin, demonstrating their mastery of game management—seen most clearly in the victory against Liverpool.

With unbelievable squad depth and confidence coursing through their veins, it's already looking like the Gunners will go back-to-back at just over the quarter mark of the 2026-27 season.

For the second consecutive season, Aston Villa faceplanted out of the starting blocks.

The West Midlanders lost three of their opening four games in 2026-27, and they only secured a point against newly promoted Hull City.

But the previous campaign, in which they earned just three points after their first five matches, offers reason for hope, with the club going on to finish in fourth place.

A similar situation could be playing out, with Villa unbeaten in their last six and securing a 2-1 victory over Manchester City.

With the loss of key players throughout the squad—including their all-time Premier League top scorer (Ollie Watkins); star midfielder (Morgan Rogers); an international-caliber center-back (Ezri Konsa); and a World Cup-winning goalkeeper (Emi Martinez)—it was always going to take some time for things to fall into place.

Thankfully, Nicolas Jackson has found his scoring boots, Johan Manzambi is delivering on his World Cup promise, and Zion Suzuki is proving dependable between the sticks (a howler against Fulham aside).

Heading into the international break, the players will be stewing over letting a pair of two-goal leads slip against Manchester United in a 4-4 draw, offering a reminder that focus is just as important as performance. A point is better than a loss, and receiving that lesson now might be a blessing in disguise in the run-up to the hectic festive period.

In Bournemouth's first six games of the season, the south-coast side picked up just three points. After a 5-1 loss to Chelsea on October 10, the Cherries were 18th and couldn't seem to shake off a severe Andoni Iraola hangover.

However, since that chastening defeat, they have secured four consecutive victories , boosting them up to seventh in the table. It seems Marco Rose has finally got his message across.

Evanilson is one goal shy of matching his Premier League scoring output from the whole of last season, while Alex Scott continues to demonstrate why he's one of the most coveted midfield talents in the Premier League. With Eli Junior Kroupi on his way back from a long-term injury, confidence will be high that the Cherries can continue their upward trajectory when they get back from the break.

There was some doom and gloom around the south-coast side heading into the campaign, with few expecting that high standards could be maintained with the departure of Iraola. However, the club has once again proved its expertise at retooling and rebuilding when prized personnel depart for pastures new.

You've got to hand it to Keith Andrews and Brentford.

Very few people are talking about the fact that they're comfortably in the top half of the league, with just two losses. That's a testimony to how the manager defied expectations last season - once people are barely surprised by your success, you've taken the club to the next level.

Standout results, such as 3-0 wins over Tottenham and Chelsea, continue to paint the G-Tech Stadium as a particularly difficult place to go. While no team has more draws than Brentford, keeping the scores level away at Leeds, Bournemouth and Aston Villa should be respected.

This is a difficult-to-beat side that, on its day, can smash the very best. And they've still got room to improve.

As everyone predicted prior to the season, Brighton & Hove Albion are Arsenal's most credible competition for the Premier League title.

Even if you were willing to ignore the potential punishment for Manchester City's alleged financial impropriety, there would still be an argument that the Seagulls have shown more staying power at the very top of the table.

Their ability to be effective against different types of opponents has been a standout factor in their success. Whether it's dominating possession to wear down more physical opponents like Brentford or disrupting and counterpunching against the likes of Arsenal and Man City, Brighton have shown they are prepared for everything the Premier League can throw at them.

It's a truly impressive coaching job by Fabian Hurzeler, particularly when you factor in that star attackers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh have yet to feature this season. Hurzeler has not only found solutions to these absences but also elevated his team in the process, and unsurprisingly, Brighton again look to have made several smart additions over the summer too.

With the team also looking likely to qualify for the next stage of the Europa Conference League, this is setting up to be a very special season down on the south coast.

Chelsea would've likely been quite happy with sitting in fifth place at this stage prior to the season. But while they deserve credit for some impressive results, including victories over Brighton & Hove Albion, Bournemouth and Everton, the manner of their defeats has been concerning.

A 3-0 loss to Brentford prior to the last international break raised questions about how high up the league this team can actually challenge, and limp defeats to Tottenham Hotspur and now Sunderland have done little to address those concerns since.

Even in a 2-0 victory against Manchester United at the end of October, Chelsea rode their luck. United missed four "big chances" before half-time, according to FotMob , after which the Blues took the lead and controlled the game following Lisandro Martínez's red card.

Injuries have been a factor, with striker João Pedro, centre-back Maxence Lacroix, goalkeeper Emi Martinez and club captain Reece James all being significant absences. Despite the club prioritizing experience in the transfer market this summer, these issues have only highlighted that Chelsea are still short on quality depth in almost every area.

It is at least encouraging that manager Xabi Alonso has been able to pick up results in spite of these problems. But Chelsea are the league's biggest overperformer on expected goals, according to FotMob , and it may be that this team has already hit its ceiling unless significant upgrades are made in January.

Of the promoted sides, Coventry City quickly began to look like the one in the most trouble.

Four straight defeats and no goals scored had the Sky Blues at the bottom of the table in early September, with crucial points also dropped in a 1-0 defeat to fellow Premier League newcomers Hull City.

But signs of life have emerged for Frank Lampard's side, with victories against Nottingham Forest, Newcastle United, and Sunderland, and 11 goals have been scored in their last seven games.

A 3-1 loss to Everton last time out will have dented confidence, with the club once again hovering perilously above the relegation zone. But with established sides struggling this season, the Sky Blues will fancy causing some upsets in their bid to cling on to Premier League status.

Ultimately, Coventry will need to invest in the January window to add proven Premier League quality to improve their odds of survival.

Crystal Palace doesn't have to pull the Frank de Boer ripcord just yet, but Pierre Sage is definitely feeling around for a parachute .

The Frenchman hasn't shown the managerial capabilities that guided Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season, with just two wins from 10 so far in his Premier League career, leaving his side rooted to the bottom of the table. The expectation is he'll get the sack, with Thomas Frank heavily rumoured to take the post .

Against Liverpool, the Eagles did look threatening, with chances to take the lead scuppered by an inspired performance by Reds goalkeeper Allison. It's clear there is something there, but they need to be more clinical. When your top scorer for the season is a left-back, Tyrick Mitchell, and he scored his team-leading two goals in a single game, there is reason to panic

Bringing in a potent striker could help everything click into place. Jean-Philippe Mateta's days at Selhurst Park look numbered (he's played just 167 minutes of league football this season, and his contract expires at the end of the campaign), and Jørgen Strand Larsen and Eddie Nketiah aren't doing enough to suggest they can compensate for the surely departing Frenchman.

With games against newly promoted sides Coventry City and Hull City on the slate after the international break, there's a serious chance of picking up a valuable six points.

After a transfer window that left them with one striker and precious little in the way of upgrades elsewhere, Everton fans could've been forgiven for a lack of optimism.

But with the team in sixth place and that striker, Thierno Barry, sitting joint-third in the league's scoring charts, it's hard to imagine how things could've gone better on the blue half of Merseyside.

It is worth noting that there is some overperformance here, with Everton sitting 11th in FotMob's expected points table , but the Toffees defend stoutly and have a 24-year-old athletic forward who has a habit of scoring important goals. Sounds like a credible European qualification contender to me, and it's reasonable to expect some further additions in January to bolster those ambitions.

With a Carabao Cup quarter-final against fourth-tier Fleetwood Town to come too, this could even be the season Everton end their 31-year trophy drought.

A summer of massive change saw Fulham swap the safe hands of Marco Silva for Álvaro Arbeloa, a manager whose stint as Real Madrid boss was less than satisfactory.

The Spaniard has brought his own ideas to Craven Cottage - a risky move in a division that can eat teams alive if sweeping alterations don't immediately work.

Arbeloa started the campaign with three defeats in a row. The writing was on the wall at that point, with calls for his sacking getting louder and the general sense that Fulham may be staring into the abyss.

Things have improved enough that there's hope. One defeat in seven matches is a marker of a team that has tightened up. One win in those seven matches is also a sign of a team that needs to find the back of the net more.

Any promoted side that only loses three times in their opening 10 games should feel very encouraged.

Hull's first season back in the Premier League started in the best way possible, with a completely dominant 2-0 victory over Manchester United that essentially set the tone for both teams in the weeks ahead.

Sergej Jakirović's side opened the campaign with three clean sheets in a row, but haven't had one since.

Even so, there's a hard-working, defensive quality in a team that knows its limitations well. Hull are never going to score buckets of goals — they're yet to hit three in a single game — but their foundation may well keep them safe.

Players such as Mohamed Belloumi, Nobel Mendy and Konstantinos Tzolakis look like a good fit at this level, with other squad members whose effort levels are through the roof to ensure Jakirović's men give a good account of themselves. They'll know the graft can't slip.

Ipswich Town will likely be satisfied with sitting in 14th with 11 points at this stage of the season after entering as heavy favorites to be relegated.

Their attack has also proved to be dangerous. They actually sit level with reigning champions Arsenal on 15 goals scored, but things look far less promising at the other end of the pitch. Ipswich have the second-worst defensive record in the league, and FotMob 's expected-goal numbers also line up with that performance.

With some teams below them looking likely to move away from trouble—Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Manchester United are all underperforming against those expected-goal metrics , while Crystal Palace's fortunes could turn around with a change in manager appearing likely—Ipswich still look set to be in the thick of a relegation scrap this season.

What will be important, then, is beating their fellow strugglers, and so far the Tractor Boys have taken points from Sunderland, Palace, Fulham, Forest and Hull City. That ability to keep picking up points in tight games is encouraging, but those defensive frailties will likely need to be addressed to keep things moving in the right direction.

Early optimism among Leeds United fans was waning slightly after a run of three points in five games, with a third-place spot in the table after four matches beginning to look like a distant memory.

But a 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur brought some life back to Elland Road, and Leeds sit a creditable ninth after 10 games played, two points back from Chelsea in fifth.

European football in 2027-28 is still an achievable dream, but manager Daniel Farke might need to ditch his typically pragmatic approach a little more often to turn draws into wins—Leeds' total of five stalemates is the joint-most in the division alongside Brentford, Hull and Manchester United.

That philosophy does have Leeds with the third-best defensive record in the top flight, with just eight goals conceded. However, only two teams (Nottingham Forest and Sunderland) have scored fewer than their total of 10.

Still, at the same point last season, the Whites were down in 16th and sizing up a relegation fight. In fact, the highest spot they achieved all season was seventh after an opening-day win against Everton, and they didn't get higher than 12th for the rest of the campaign.

The question now is whether consolidating their top-flight status or pushing on for an unexpected European berth is the goal. The former might be the more sensible path, but the supporters will no doubt be dreaming of a first appearance in an international club competition since 2002-03.

Summarizing Liverpool's season so far depends on whether you're a glass-half-full or glass-half-empty kind of person.

The good news: Alexander Isak has more than doubled his Premier League scoring tally of last season in just nine appearances; Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister look much improved; Jeremy Jacquet appears to be the heir-apparent to Virgil van Dijk; and Liverpool's youth ranks are being relied upon more than shuffling players into unfamiliar positions to fill gaps.

The bad news: Florian Wirtz still looks a little lost in the Premier League; Andoni Iraola hasn't figured out how this team can break down low blocks; injuries remain a persistent problem; Liverpool continue to concede first and early; and the Reds are already nine points back from league leaders Arsenal.

The mood at Anfield is certainly far more positive than in the last weeks under Arne Slot's guidance, but Iraola's methods still haven't quite taken root, despite occasional signs of his high-pressing, energetic football.

Comfort can be taken from the Spaniard's start to life in the Premier League, with his Bournemouth side taking 10 games to secure their first win in 2023-24. Five wins in the same amount of time at Liverpool is a much better record, and the Cherries finished that season in a remarkable 12th place.

The best may still be to come for the Reds, but patience is often in short supply among football fans. For now, it's a middling grade for a middling season.

Three losses in a row have underlined an awful period for Manchester City, who may well not even be in the division next season once the punishment for the 114 charges is delivered.

The early defiance in the wake of that verdict has subsided; the fans dressed as bananas are no longer baiting others with win after win.

Truth is, even forgetting what may be right around the corner for Enzo Maresca's side, Man City are a step down when compared to champions Arsenal. Five behind in the title race with 10 matches played is a sizeable gap that doesn't look like it's going to slow down.

Maresca hasn't quite found a working formula in defence — City have conceded as many as 16th-placed Nottingham Forest — while the cutting and changing of players such as Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden isn't helping the team settle. If Man City aren't winning, they're failing.

Do Manchester United even deserve a grade? If this were school, they'd be held back a year…or 13.

The inevitable has happened, and Michael Carrick has been proven to be out of his depth after a bright run as interim boss at the tail end of last season. Jim Ratcliffe, Jason Wilcox and United's band of idiots have (so far) decided that a manager who has one win from 10 matches is worth keeping on.

That, of course, after they left him hanging in the transfer market without providing the squad depth he desperately needs.

In all honesty, Carrick isn't the problem. He's just the latest person who happens to be in charge. INEOS could fuse the minds of Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola and Arsène Wenger into a manager-ultron, but they'd still forget to program the function that stops their invention from falling apart at least once a week.

Comebacks against Roma and Aston Villa don't hide the fact that things feel different at United right now, even after all the frustration since Fergie called time on his career. The Red Devils are in the relegation zone and legitimately flirting with disaster.

New manager Matthias Jaissle got off to a flyer with Newcastle. The opening day draw with Liverpool was followed by a victory over Spurs and a draw with Bournemouth — that's a very tough start well navigated.

The issue is, the Magpies were walloped away at Leeds and Coventry just after that, whilst also losing to Villa and Everton at home. Jaissle is actually under some pressure with the team treading water in 12th, and it feels like it could go either way.

There's no need to get too crazy just yet. This is a young manager, in a new league, with a squad that isn't his own. While Jaissle needs to find some kind of balance in the team, particularly down the middle, he should be afforded time to build a squad that fits his style better.

Prior to this weekend, things looked dark for Nottingham Forest. After a 2-0 defeat to Brentford, which saw the team suffer its fourth loss in five games, manager Oliver Glasner raised the possibility of his own departure after only joining in the summer.

"We have to change it. And if you can't change it, we need different personnel," he told reporters . "And if the club doesn't want to change it, they need a different manager. I'm desperate to change it. Desperate."

That desperation appeared to be transmitted to his players, who simply outbattled Manchester City on the way to a 3-1 victory on Saturday.

Glasner's Crystal Palace team often looked more comfortable playing against opponents like Manchester City, who are happy to leave space to be attacked, and he may need to continue to look for solutions against opponents who are happier to play more conservatively.

After the defeat to Brentford, though, Glasner highlighted his team being outrun by opponents as a factor in their struggles. And if there is one encouraging takeaway from the Manchester City victory, it's that his team certainly doesn't lack the desire to outwork teams.

Sunderland's 1-0 victory over Chelsea on Sunday sent them into the international break on a high after a fairly miserable few weeks.

Serious questions have been asked of manager Régis Le Bris over a seven-game winless run in the league, during which time the Black Cats were also beaten 2-0 at home by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

After that game, Le Bris told reporters he had spoken with owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus and appeared optimistic he retained the support of club leadership.

Sunday's result may still end up just delaying the inevitable, but Sunderland showed they can be a physical test for anyone. The difficulty will be continuing to summon that level of intensity amid a challenging schedule for a squad that looks a little short of the depth required for the challenge of balancing European and domestic football.

With the team on course to progress in Europe and a Carabao Cup quarter-final on the horizon, there are still bright spots to cling onto. But nobody wants to be in a relegation fight, and Le Bris may pay the price if his team's league form doesn't improve.

The 1-0 defeat against Leeds United on Saturday brought Tottenham Hotspur crashing back down to earth after a run of three straight wins finally had the team looking up the table again after spending two seasons struggling around the relegation zone.

Those results were encouraging, especially after a winless start to the season that saw Spurs fail to score in their first four games, but it is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook this team's struggles in attack.

Spurs sit 17th in expected goals scored, according to FotMob , and they are still reliant on set pieces to break down stubborn defences. As The Athletic's Liam Tharme noted in an article prior to the Leeds defeat, "[Spurs] rank second for the proportion of goals from set pieces (40 percent, only behind Leeds United's 44.4 percent) and third for the share of expected goals generated from dead balls (32.4 percent)."

The win against Chelsea in late October provided a look at what Spurs could be at their best: a dominant possession team that stifles opponents both with and without the ball. But even in a game where almost everything went right for them, their victory required a goalkeeping error from Chelsea's Mike Penders and a wonder strike from Mathys Tel, who now also looks likely to miss time through injury.

After spending over $400 million on transfers this summer, there were suggestions Spurs could challenge for Champions League qualification again this season. But after 10 games, it looks like further investment will be required to fix a struggling front line.

articles.title: College Football Playoff projections: Could Big Ten and SEC only get 6 teams in the 12-team field?
articles.summary: The two big conferences have earned 15 of the 24 combined spots in the first two years of the 12-team playoff.
articles.body:
How possible is it that the Big Ten and SEC get fewer teams in the College Football Playoff than they did in 2024 and 2025?

Two seasons ago, the two conferences combined to occupy seven of the 12 spots in the field. A year ago, they got eight, as five SEC teams made the postseason.

Could that number be down to six in 2026? There's certainly a scenario if Texas Tech and Wake Forest keep reeling off wins behind Utah and Miami.

Since it's officially College Football Playoff rankings season, here's our first official prediction at what the field will look like in early December.

No. 1 Georgia (8-1, projected SEC champion)

The Bulldogs have games remaining against Missouri and South Carolina before a home game against Georgia Tech to end the season. There's a scenario where Georgia can have a spot in the SEC title game wrapped up with a win against the Tigers in Week 11. The Bulldogs were utterly dominant in their third game against Ole Miss in 15 months and look like the favorites for the national title.

No. 2 Utah (9-0, projected Big 12 champion)

Is Utah's trip to Arizona the best game of Week 11? The Wildcats are 7-2 and their only losses have come on the road at BYU and at Texas Tech. The tiebreakers won't be in their favor, but they can shove themselves back into the mix for the Big 12 championship game with an upset win over the Utes. Utah, meanwhile, has TCU and West Virginia remaining after heading to Tucson.

We're fascinated to see how far the committee vaults Notre Dame in the rankings on Tuesday night. After all, the Fighting Irish did exactly what the panel asked them to do. With games against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse remaining, Notre Dame is a heavy favorite to finish the season at 11-1 and sit back and watch conference championship weekend far more comfortably than it did in 2025.

If Notre Dame loses one of its final three games, however, the committee could again move them toward the bubble.

No. 4 Indiana (8-1, projected Big Ten champion)

The Hoosiers were off in Week 10 and we'll see in Week 11 what the quarterback situation is like and if the offense can get unlocked with either Josh Hoover or Grant Wilson under center. Indiana may look to overpower USC's defense with a bruising run game either way. After the Trojans visit, Indiana has Washington and Purdue before a likely appearance in the Big Ten title game.

No. 5 Miami (8-1, projected ACC champion) vs. No. 12 Boise State (8-1, projected Pac-12 champion)

The Hurricanes should still be considered the prohibitive favorite to win the ACC, but their game against Duke on Saturday suddenly gets more intriguing with the Blue Devils 7-2 and on a tear. A lot of college football fans across the country are going to get their first extended look at Duke RB Nate Sheppard. He's rushed for 1,189 yards and 17 TDs on just 191 carries.

The Broncos routed Colorado State in Week 10 with backup QB Max Cutforth going 16-of-19 for 317 yards and four touchdowns. Oregon State visits Boise in Week 11 — ESPN's "College GameDay" will be in Idaho — but the Beavers are on a two-game losing streak.

No. 6 UCLA (9-0, at-large) vs. No. 11 Wake Forest (8-1, at-large)

The Bruins just keep taking care of business. UCLA outscored Minnesota by 14 in the second half in a 34-20 win in Minneapolis as Ty Dieffenbach threw for 303 yards on just eight completions. As it stands now, Oregon and USC — who UCLA plays in Week 13 — are the only ranked teams the Bruins will face all regular season. The committee signaled strongly that it cares about strength of schedule. That's irrelevant as long as UCLA keeps winning. But what happens if the Bruins drop a game over the final three weeks of the season?

We've got the Demon Deacons in the field as we like their chances to be Miami's opponent in the ACC title game. Wake has games at SMU and Georgia Tech along with a home game against Duke remaining. If the Deacs are 11-2 with both losses coming to the Hurricanes, how can they be left out?

No. 7 Alabama (7-2, at-large) vs. No. 10 Texas Tech (8-1, at-large)

The Crimson Tide could move up to No. 4 on Tuesday night and are heavy favorites in their final three regular season games. But how far could they slip in the rankings if they finish 10-3 with another loss to Georgia in the SEC title game? It's feasible the committee may not move Alabama much at all if that happens. For now, we've got the Tide slotted here, and this is about as low as they'll be if they win out over the final three weeks.

Texas Tech simply needs to keep winning. The Red Raiders' defense was gashed Saturday night by West Virginia in their win and they now head to Stillwater to face an Oklahoma State team that put up 49 points in the first half at Kansas State.

No. 8 Texas (7-2, at-large) vs. No. 9 Tennessee (7-2, at-large)

The Longhorns ripped off 21 straight points in the second half to put Missouri away 34-20 after Arch Manning's controversial fumble that looked like an incomplete pass. Texas heads to LSU in Week 11, but then has games against Arkansas and Texas A&M to finish the season. Even if Texas loses to LSU and finishes 9-3, we have a hard time seeing how the Longhorns are out of the playoff.

Tennessee gets LSU the week after the Longhorns and draws Texas A&M in Week 11. The Volunteers were ruthless in a 28-point win over Kentucky on Saturday and that head-to-head victory could likely end up being crucial in determining the final few playoff spots.

articles.title: Ohio State Coach Reportedly Fired After Loss to Oregon 'After Allowing a Critical Fake Punt'
articles.summary: Ohio State's 41-28 loss to Oregon on Saturday was costly in more ways than one.
articles.body:
Ohio State's 41-28 loss to Oregon on Saturday was costly in more ways than one.

Per ESPN's Adam Rittenberg , the Buckeyes fired special teams coordinator Robby Discher "after allowing a critical fake punt conversion" in Saturday's loss to the Ducks, which dropped their record to 6-3 this season.

Discher was hired as Ohio State's special teams coordinator just nine months ago following his run at Illinois, where he held the same role and also served as tight ends coach. He also previously coached special teams at Tulane and Toledo.

On Saturday against the Ducks, the Buckeyes held a 14-3 lead in the second quarter when Oregon executed a fake punt with Teitum Tuioti throwing a jump pass to fellow defensive lineman Matayo Uiagalelei for a 30-yard gain. The team went on to score a touchdown, starting a run of 38 unanswered points.

After Ohio State's second straight loss, head coach Ryan Day said he planned to "evaluate everything."

"Getting off the field there before the fake punt would have been a huge stop and enabled for us to get the ball on offense and eat up some more clock there in the second quarter," Day said. "But it didn't happen. So I've got to evaluate everything and try to come in [Sunday] and figure out with the staff the things that we're just coming up short on and figure out how to adjust those things. And I think it all starts with the staff. And then it goes to the players. So there needs to be accountability for all of it. And then we go from there."

Day also lamented the Buckeyes' penalties, several of which were on special teams. Rittenberg noted that Ohio State ranks 102nd nationally in special teams efficiency this season.

"The penalties are a killer," Day said. "At the end of the day as a coach, you've got to look yourself in the mirror and find out why that's happening."

The Buckeyes' third loss of the season could be enough to end their College Football Playoff hopes, but they will try to finish strong in their final three regular-season games, starting with Saturday's matchup against Northwestern (6-3).

articles.title: Zidane convoca para la selección francesa a un jugador de la segunda división alemana
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador galo ha llamado al joven defensa Saël Kumbedi, de 21 años, que milita en el Wolfsburgo de la segunda división alemana para paliar la baja de Kalulu
articles.summary: El seleccionador galo ha llamado al joven defensa Saël Kumbedi, de 21 años, que milita en el Wolfsburgo de la segunda división alemana para paliar la baja de Kalulu
articles.body: Zinedine Zidane ofreció el pasado viernes su segunda lista oficial como seleccionador de la selección francesa. En ella, Mbappé lidera una convocatoria repleta de bajas. Y como podía esperarse, otra más ha llegado antes incluso de la concentración del equipo. Pierre Kalulu, el defensa de la Juventus, no podrá estar con el combinado nacional y el técnico galo ha sorprendido con la llamada de un jugador de la 2. Bundesliga, Saël Kumbedi, que milita en el Wolfsburgo. Se trata de la primera convocatoria de Kumbedi, que formaba parte de la lista de los sub-21 de Gérald Baticle y que finalmente se incorporará a la absoluta. Kalulu, de 26 años, que cuenta ya con cinco partidos internacionales, sufrió una lesión en los isquiotibiales en el partido que la Juventus de Turín disputó este domingo contra la Fiorentina. Cabe recordar que Francia se verá las caras este jueves contra Italia en Milán y el próximo domingo cerrará frente a Turquía en Burdeos la primera fase de la Liga de las Naciones que la tiene encuadrada en el grupo 1A, el cual lidera con tres y cuatro puntos de ventaja respecto a italianos y belgas, respectivamente, a falta de los dos últimos compromisos.

articles.title: Felicia Schröder conquista el Golden Girl
articles.standfirst: La joven delantera del Real Madrid es reconocida como la mejor Sub21 de Europa
articles.summary: La joven centrocampista del Barcelona es reconocida como la mejor Sub21 de Europa
articles.body: El futuro se vislumbra absolutamente brillante en el Real Madrid femenino: Felicia Schröder (Suecia, 2007), flamante fichaje del conjunto blanco el pasado verano, se corona con el Golden Girl a mejor jugadora joven de Europa. La joven delantera del conjunto blanco, a sus todavía 19 años, sucede a Michelle Agyemang tras imponerse en la votación final a las jugadoras del Barcelona Clara Serrajordi (2007), Sydney Schertenleib (2007) y Giulia Galli (2008). Todas las ganadoras del Golden Girl (2022-2026): La perla del Real Madrid destacó la pasada temporada con el BK Häcken sueco, con el que conquistó la Liga de su país, además de ser determinante en la conquista de la primera edición de la Women's Europa Cup, de la que fue máxima goleadora con 8 tantos. La internacional sueca jugó 41 partidos con su equipo, anotando 43 goles y repartiendo 12 asistencias. Además, jugó cinco partidos internacionales en los que anotó otros tres tantos. Se convierte, tras Linda Caicedo, en la segunda madridista en conquistar el galardón.

articles.title: College Football Playoff, ESPN agree to 5-year, $1.7 billion deal expanding field to 24 teams starting in 2027
articles.summary: The CFP field will have 12 teams this year, before doubling in 2027.
articles.body:
ESPN and the College Football Playoff (CFP) have agreed to a 5-year deal to expand the playoff from 12 to 24 teams.

The deal, worth $1.7 billion per ESPN's Heather Dinich , keeps ESPN as the broadcast partner.

"The decision to expand was driven by a desire to increase opportunities for FBS programs, student-athletes and fan bases to participate in the Playoff and have a chance to play for the CFP National Championship, while new scheduling standards incentivize institutions to schedule more compelling non-conference matchups during the regular season. The expanded format will feature 16 on-campus Playoff games, which will bring Playoff football to more students and local fans while providing a positive impact for campus communities."

CFP executive director Rich Clark also commented about the expansion and the hopes for what it means for the sport and fans.

"We will make the 24-team Playoff spectacular for the fans, student-athletes, their institutions and all our stakeholders. That is our commitment. Our organization delivers a world-class championship experience at our games and our events, and this promise will continue under the new format. 23 games of Playoff football, featuring 24 ranked teams going head-to-head for the right to be crowned the true national champion. We are also thrilled to continue our broadcast partnership with ESPN, which has been a terrific partner of the CFP since its inception. Like the CFP, ESPN celebrates everything that makes the sport of college football so great. The promotion, storytelling and innovation ESPN brings to the CFP, college football fans and the sport in general, is second to none. We know that level of excellence will continue as we embark on this journey to a 24-team format. We'd like to thank our media advisors at CAA for their work and support getting this agreement completed. This would not have been possible without their guidance and expertise."

"We will make the 24-team Playoff spectacular for the fans, student-athletes, their institutions and all our stakeholders. That is our commitment. Our organization delivers a world-class championship experience at our games and our events, and this promise will continue under the new format. 23 games of Playoff football, featuring 24 ranked teams going head-to-head for the right to be crowned the true national champion.

We are also thrilled to continue our broadcast partnership with ESPN, which has been a terrific partner of the CFP since its inception. Like the CFP, ESPN celebrates everything that makes the sport of college football so great. The promotion, storytelling and innovation ESPN brings to the CFP, college football fans and the sport in general, is second to none. We know that level of excellence will continue as we embark on this journey to a 24-team format. We'd like to thank our media advisors at CAA for their work and support getting this agreement completed. This would not have been possible without their guidance and expertise."

Talk of the CFP expanding to 24 teams gained steam in September, when the CFP and ESPN began negotiating after the College Football Playoff triggered a 30-day negotiating window .

The CFP released a statement in early October confirming that talks with ESPN were ongoing.

"Constructive discussions with ESPN continued this week. We have enjoyed a strong partnership with ESPN since our inception and are appreciative of the productive dialogue we have had throughout the negotiating period and continuing over the last several days. We will provide additional updates on the matters of future format and media rights when appropriate."

A Dec. 1 deadline loomed to close a deal in time to affect the 2027 CFP format. This is only the third year of a 12-team format following 10 years of the 4-team playoff format that ended in 2023.

The report also added that this expansion to 24 teams eliminates Power 4 conference championship games, but it didn't expand on that aspect.

Dinich also mentioned some key dates for the 2027 season. "Week 0" will no longer happen, and the season will begin with Week 1 the week before Labor Day and will end the weekend of Thanksgiving.

Selection Day for the 2027 CFP will be on Nov. 28, 2027, and the national championship game will still be held on Jan. 24, 2028. The Army-Navy game will still occur and keep its standalone window, but will now be held the weekend that Power 4 conference championships were held.

The 24-team field is expected to include 19 at-large teams and the Power 4 champions. If there are no conference championship games, though, each league will have to decide how to crown its champion. Currently, that is expected to be through a combination of regular-season standings and tiebreakers.

The final team will still be the highest-ranked team in the Group of 6. On3's Brett McMurphy reported that the Group of 6 hasn't decided whether to eliminate its conference championship games.

Currently, Notre Dame gets an auto-bid if it finishes in the CFP's top-12, but this expansion would eliminate any guarantee for the Fighting Irish.

The CFP currently ranks 25 teams each week, and that is expected to continue, but could expand to a 30-team ranking to show which teams are in the hunt down the stretch of the season.

The 24-team format would see the top eight seeds receive a bye. The first two rounds of the playoff tournament would take place at the campus of the higher seed. The quarterfinals and semifinals will still be contested via the New Year's Six Bowls (Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Peach, Cotton and Orange) leading up to the national championship.

articles.title: England: Kane and Bellingham air strong views in World Cup review
articles.summary: England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting.
articles.body:
England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting.

As BBC Sport reported in September, the Football Association (FA) process included canvassing the opinions of the squad - and it has emerged that took place at a 'full and frank' meeting with head coach Thomas Tuchel at the start of the September international break.

BBC Sport has been told the squad feel that now they have been able to have their say, they can move on from their heartbreak in Atlanta on 15 July.

And this was demonstrated in the last international break when England, after a narrow defeat by Spain in the first game, went on to win the next three matches impressively.

Burn replaces injured Guehi in England squad

Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel?

'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up

The ramifications of the Argentina defeat, or perhaps more pertinently, the circumstances, meant some of the squad held grievances, with those feelings lingering and even growing throughout the summer.

In particular there was unhappiness about how Tuchel told them to approach the closing stages of the game after Anthony Gordon had given them a 55th-minute advantage.

Enzo Fernandez struck an equaliser with five minutes left, before Lautaro Martinez headed in a stoppage-time winner.

As reported by BBC Sport at the time, a number of senior England players held misgivings at Tuchel's instructions for the closing stages of the Argentina loss, believing the approach was too negative and defensive.

Hindsight, of course, is 20/20. England appeared to retreat in the closing stages of the last-16 tie against Mexico earlier in the tournament - but successfully defended a 3-2 lead to reach the quarter-finals to trigger scenes of joy at the iconic Azteca Stadium.

Nevertheless, certain players felt let down by the team's apparent pragmatism during the closing stages of the loss to Argentina amid a sense that going for the South Americans' jugular would have provided greater success.

Inevitably, the game against Argentina emerged as a key theme at the squad discussion.

It is understood that Tuchel pointed to the quality of the opposition as a key factor on why they eventually succumbed to two late Argentina goals.

There is, of course, merit to that argument. Lionel Messi was in the opposition team after all.

That said, it was not an argument the players in the meeting were prepared to universally accept.

There is a strongly held view within the England squad that their team, man-for-man, was superior to Argentina, who had 38-year-old Nicolas Otamendi on the field for the closing 18 minutes of the game.

All players were afforded an opportunity to air their personal views during the meeting.

As you would expect, captain Harry Kane was strong and forthright with his views.

Jude Bellingham, too, is said to have been particularly candid in expressing his belief that this current crop of England players were more than capable of continuing to take the game to Argentina.

Bellingham's contribution to the meeting is said to have underlined his growing influence within the England squad, with many believing the Real Madrid midfielder will become the team's captain once Kane is no longer in the picture.

If the air needed to be cleared after the World Cup then it appears those honest discussions at the end of September did the trick.

Barring the 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in their first Nations League fixture in September, England have bounced back from the loss to Argentina emphatically - scoring 12 goals without conceding in three fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia.

Similarly, the fluctuating relationship between Bellingham and Tuchel seems to have improved, too.

"It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place," Tuchel said last week.

"I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways."

We will get a clearer idea of how 'Tuchel 2.0' is progressing in the next few days when England host Croatia on Thursday and travel to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday.

articles.title: Michael Carrick: Manchester United yet to make decision on whether to sack manager
articles.summary: Manchester United's board are yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future, despite the club's worst start to a campaign in 40 years.
articles.body:
Manchester United's board is yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick's future.

The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.

The draw was Carrick's third match in charge since the board decided to give the 45-year-old more time to improve the side's form after a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October.

The board felt Carrick - and the players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around, while the heirachy were also aware that November's two-week break would offer an opportunity to reassess the situation in a calmer manner.

They are determined to do exactly that, knowing the results - one win, one draw and one defeat - and performances United have delivered in the past three games offer a mixed view of Carrick's tenure.

Conceding eight goals, winning only once and dropping into the relegation zone are obvious negatives. However, it is also felt fighting back from two goals down three times over the past two games showed that the players remain behind Carrick.

United's heirachy explored the possibility of replacing Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth last month, with ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann considered.

Carrick said after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that he would not step down, but chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will be influential in the decision whether to keep the former Middlesbrough boss.

United travel to arch rivals Liverpool on 22 November in their first match after the international break, with Carrick's side in 18th place in the Premier League.

With just one league win so far this term, it is United's lowest position having played 10 matches since the 1986-87 campaign.

Following the Anfield trip, five of United's next seven league opponents are in the bottom half of the league. This includes the four other sides currently in the bottom five, with meetings against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, all at Old Trafford.

Whether Carrick keeps his job or not, United will continue to struggle unless they stop conceding goals with such regularity.

Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich have let in more than United's 19 league goals.

They have conceded 15 times in the past three matches in all competitions. Their only clean sheet this term came against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK in the Champions League.

"All the Premier League teams, whether they play home or away against Manchester United, fancy their chances because you can open them up and score goals," former United assistant boss Rene Meulensteen told BBC Radio Five Live.

"No matter what combination you find it's just not good enough. I think Michael Carrick will be constantly puzzled as to what back four he can play because there's no certainty they can keep a clean sheet."

Full-back Diogo Dalot took the brunt of fan ire at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Huge cheers greeted his number being shown to confirm he was being replaced, which then turned to boos when he reached the dugout.

Substitute Joshua Zirkzee, who suffered similar treatment when he was replaced after half an hour of a home defeat to Newcastle in December 2024, made a point of hugging Dalot as he made his way back to the bench.

Asked if it was time to take Dalot out of the firing line, Carrick urged caution.

"We've got to be careful with that," he said.

"I understand the frustration and I understand the disappointment of the supporters, I get it. We're all frustrated, we're all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

"Diogo gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions and played really well at times.

"He gives a penalty away. He knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better. He made a mistake. But I like what he brings to the team. He cares an awful lot and he's giving everything."

articles.title: Varapalo para el Málaga: Rafita estará al menos tres meses de baja
articles.standfirst: El conjunto malacitano recibe un golpe importante en uno de los momentos más delicados de la temporada
articles.summary: El conjunto malacitano recibe un golpe importante en uno de los momentos más delicados de la temporada
articles.body: Rafita, que se había convertido en uno de los futbolistas más destacados del equipo, estará apartado de los terrenos de juego durante un periodo estimado de entre tres y cuatro meses. Según ha podido saber Radio MARCA Málaga, el lateral axárquico afronta una recuperación que podría prolongarse hasta bien entrado 2027. La lesión también le obliga a renunciar a su convocatoria con la selección española sub-21. Las señales de alarma aparecieron durante el encuentro del pasado sábado ante el Racing de Santander. Rafita notó un pinchazo y terminó tendido sobre el césped. Aunque trató de reincorporarse al partido, las dificultades para caminar con normalidad y la evidente cojera que presentaba en su pierna izquierda hicieron imposible su continuidad. Las sensaciones iniciales ya apuntaban a una lesión importante y las pruebas médicas han terminado confirmando los peores pronósticos. El diagnóstico señala una lesión en el tendón conjunto de los músculos isquiotibiales de la pierna izquierda. Se trata de una dolencia de consideración que guarda similitudes con la sufrida por Éder Militao en el Real Madrid a finales de 2025, cuando el central brasileño tuvo que afrontar varios meses de recuperación. En Martiricos son conscientes de la importancia de una baja que afecta directamente a uno de los futbolistas con mayor peso en el rendimiento del equipo. El club blanquiazul ha confirmado la lesión a través de un comunicado médico. Rafita sufrió molestias en la zona de los isquiotibiales de la pierna izquierda durante el partido disputado el sábado 7 de noviembre frente al Real Racing Club, una circunstancia que le impidió terminar el encuentro. Las pruebas diagnósticas realizadas este lunes en el Hospital Quirónsalud Málaga han determinado que el futbolista padece una lesión en el tendón conjunto de los músculos isquiotibiales. La entidad no ha establecido plazos oficiales para su regreso y señala que su disponibilidad estará condicionada por la evolución de la lesión.

articles.title: Cientos de aficionados, 13 jugadores de la sub-21 y un emotivo recuerdo a Jesús de Miguel en Las Rozas
articles.standfirst: Miles de personas acompañaron a la selección en la sesión de este lunes.
articles.summary: Miles de personas acompañaron a la selección en la sesión de este lunes.
articles.body: Ni el festivo, ni el fresquito, ni la lluvia pudieron con las ganas de los aficionados de la selección española de disfrutar de los campeones del mundo. Primero fueron las colas y, en cuanto se abrieron las puertas, llegaron las carreras de los más pequeños para ocupar los puestos de privilegio de las gradas, los que dan acceso a la foto y el autógrafo con el que tanto soñaban. La sesión se inició con los jugadores y el cuerpo técnico recordando la figura de Jesús de Miguel, por quien guardaron un emotivo minuto de silencio. Unai Simón portaba un ramo de flores y Ferran Torres una camiseta de la selección con el número y el dorsal del futbolista del Tenerife. Pese a la ausencia de jugadores de la talla de Lamine, quien se espera que esté disponible para el partido del domingo ante Inglaterra, los más pequeños -y los no tanto- animaron, cantaron y disfrutaron de los jugadores. Se trata de la última sesión abierta al público de este año. Un año en el que la selección se proclamó campeona del mundo. Por eso cientos de chavales ya lucían las dos estrellas en la camiseta que ahora acompañan con el autógrafo de su ídolo. En la sesión también participaron 13 jugadores de la selección española sub-21: Gonzalo García, Carlos Espí, Rodrigo Mendoza, Thiago Pitarch, Cristhian Mosquera, Manu González, Ángel Ortiz, Javi Hernández, Yarek Gasiorowski, David Mella, Pablo García, Bruno Iribarne y Salva Esquivel.

articles.title: Ben White: England defender says people don't know 'full story' behind his self-inflicted exile from national team
articles.summary: Arsenal defender Ben White says people don't know the "full story" behind his decision to previously make himself unavailable for England selection - but says he would make the same decision again.
articles.body:
Arsenal defender Ben White says people do not know the "full story" behind his decision to previously make himself unavailable for England selection - but says he would make the same decision again.

White, who has been named in Thomas Tuchel's squad for upcoming Nations League fixtures, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons.

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign, and was booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Tuchel.

Asked by BBC Radio 5 live's football correspondent John Murray what he would say to people who define his England career by what happened in Qatar, White said: "I think obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that.

"It's been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now."

White is now 29 and asked if he would have done anything differently in hindsight, he added: "No, I don't think I would.

"Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.

"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.

"So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on."

White came on for his first England appearance since 2022 in March's 1-1 draw with Uruguay and was booed by some supporters before he scored but also gave away the penalty that led to the visitors' equaliser.

After that, Chelsea midfielder Jordan Henderson said he and his fellow England players would always support White, while Tuchel said recently that the defender deserves "a new chapter" and "positive feedback from the crowd".

Asked how he dealt with the emotions of that night at Wembley, White added: "Before the game I was thinking 'don't not stand out, but [take it] nice and easy'.

"Then I came on and obviously got booed, then I scored, then I gave away a penalty.

"So, it was obviously full of emotions that night, [but] it was a good night."

England play Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before taking on world champions Spain in Madrid three days later.

White is looking to add to his six England caps in this international break and said: "It is obviously an amazing privilege to be called up.

"The feeling is the same every time you do get this chance to play for England. It's one I am really looking forward to this week."

images.caption: Image caption, Ben White made his first England appearance in more than three years against Uruguay in March

articles.title: Raúl, 32 años después
articles.summary: La opinión de Chisco García
articles.body: Seguro que ninguno de los presentes en el Carlos Tartiere aquella tarde del 6 de septiembre de 1994, cuando el Real Madrid de Jorge Valdano visitó Oviedo para disputar un amistoso relacionado con el fichaje de Robert Prosinecki, imaginó que, 32 años después, aquel joven delantero casi desconocido acabaría sentado en el banquillo azul. Era Raúl González Blanco, que empezaba a asomarse al primer equipo blanco y dejó su sello con un gol. El fútbol escribe historias que ni el mejor guionista inventaría. Raúl afronta ahora otro desafío: dirigir a un histórico que necesita recuperar su sitio en Primera división tras un año de frustración colectiva. No lo tendrá fácil, entre otras cosas porque muchos juzgarán al entrenador a través del recuerdo del delantero que tantas tardes de gloria dio al Real Madrid. Y son dos profesiones muy distintas. La figura de Raúl no puede generar más que ilusión. Quienes desconfíen de su contratación porque sólo ha entrenado en la cantera madridista, deberían valorar cuánto acumuló durante una de las carreras más brillantes de nuestro fútbol. Conoció técnicos de todos los perfiles, convivió con la máxima exigencia y aprendió a soportar la presión donde cada empate parece una derrota. De esas experiencias habrá extraído lecciones que ahora podrá trasladar al vestuario azul. El sábado, ante el Girona, empezaremos a descubrir cuánto hay del futbolista que fue en el entrenador que quiere ser. Jesús Martínez, presidente del Grupo Pachuca, nunca ha ocultado su preferencia por equipos ambiciosos, valientes y dispuestos a asumir riesgos. Tampoco su admiración por las grandes figuras del fútbol internacional. Raúl pertenece a ese grupo de elegidos. Por eso, la confianza de la propiedad parece casi ilimitada. Sólo una catástrofe de resultados podría quebrar una apuesta que va más allá de lo deportivo. Los clubes históricos necesitan ganar partidos, pero también que se reconozca su grandeza y que su nombre recupere el lugar que merece. Con Raúl, el Real Oviedo vuelve a cobrar protagonismo nacional e internacional. Se habla de los azules mucho más allá de Asturias y de nuestras fronteras. Es cierto que ahora las miradas estarán más pendientes del banquillo que del césped, pero quizá sea ahí donde empiece a construirse algo importante. 32 años después, aquel muchacho que comenzaba a escribir su leyenda de blanco regresa al Carlos Tartiere para intentar escribir otra historia. Esta vez, de azul. Y con toda la responsabilidad sobre sus espaldas.

images.caption: Raúl, celebrando un gol contra el Oviedo.

articles.title: "Hoy la afición amarilla abraza a la blanquiazul"
articles.standfirst: Emotivo acto en memoria de Jesús de Miguel en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria
articles.summary: Emotivo acto en memoria de Jesús de Miguel en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria
articles.body: La rivalidad entre Las Palmas y Tenerife ha quedado a un lado para dar paso al cariño, el respeto y la unión del fútbol canario. Desde que falleció Jesús de Miguel, los clubes y sus aficiones han estado hombro sobre lágrima. Las aficiones de ambos clubes se han unido este lunes para rendir homenaje al futbolista, en un emotivo acto celebrado en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria, antes del encuentro que enfrenta al conjunto amarillo con el CD Eldense. Un gesto cargado de simbolismo, precisamente en la puerta que coincide con el dorsal que lucía el delantero tinerfeñista. En la puerta 9 se ha leído un manifiesto por la presidenta de Peñas de la UD Las Palmas, Guacimara Sosa. Un mensaje lleno de cariño y afecto con frases reseñables como "hoy la afición amarilla abraza a la blanquiazul porque la vida, el respeto y el dolor están por encima de nuestra rivalidad". Además de que Las Palmas hoy jugará con su tercera equipación (coincide con los colores del Tenerife), el club ha diseñado un brazalete especial para la ocasión. Un brazalete que portará el tinerfeño Kirian, y en el que figura el dibujo de Jesús de Miguel celebrando un gol, los escudos de la UD Las Palmas y el CD Tenerife y una frase que reza Jesús de Miguel siempre en nuestro recuerdo.

images.caption: La afición de la UD Las Palmas y del CD Tenerife, unidas en la puerta 9 del Gran Canaria. UD LAS PALMAS

articles.title: FA Cup second-round draw: Wimborne to host Bradford City
articles.summary: Seventh-tier side Wimborne Town will host League One Bradford City in the second round of the FA Cup, while former winners Leicester City will visit National League South side Dover Athletic.
articles.body:
Seventh-tier side Wimborne Town will host League One Bradford City in the second round of the FA Cup.

The Magpies shocked Crawley Town on Sunday in the first round, scoring twice to dump their League Two opponents out of the competition and progress to the second round for the first time.

The Bantams thumped Marine 7-0 on Saturday and sit seventh in the third tier.

Elsewhere in the draw, former Premier League and FA Cup winners Leicester City will travel to National League South side Dover Athletic.

Fresh from beating Sholing 6-0 , Salisbury FC of the sixth tier will face League One Blackpool at the Ray Mac Stadium.

National League side AFC Fylde will host Jack Wilshere's Luton Town and seventh-tier Guiseley AFC will take on Notts County of League One.

The second round will take place on the weekend starting Friday, 4 December.

Second-round winners will receive £79,500 in prize money, with £21,200 for the losing clubs.
